title: Salbutamol tolerance to bronchoprotection: course of onset
authors: Stewart SL, Martin AL, Davis BE, Cockcroft DW
population: Thirteen people with mild asthma at the University of Saskatchewan; randomised double-blind placebo-controlled crossover of seven twice-daily doses of salbutamol 200 µg or placebo, with methacholine challenge 10 minutes after the first, third, fifth and seventh doses
funder: not read in the article: the full text requires a subscription. The registry names the University of Saskatchewan as lead sponsor and responsible party, with no collaborator listed.
result: A single dose of salbutamol shifted the methacholine PC20 about fivefold, from a geometric mean of 2.1 to 10.7 mg/ml. Bronchoprotection peaked on day 2 after the third dose, was trending down after the fifth dose and on day 4, after the seventh dose, was significantly lower than its peak (p = 0.001); PC20 under placebo did not change over the 4 days.
